# Ship post-release branch cleanup fails non-deterministically (shared /tmp report path / concurrent agents)

## Problem statement

The ship skill's post-release branch cleanup (`runPostReleaseCleanup` in
`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) fails non-deterministically in a
multi-agent (herdr) environment because it reads and writes a **fixed shared
temp path** (`${os.tmpdir()}/cleanup-summary.json`): when two release/cleanup
processes run concurrently, one clobbers the other's report, so the run logs
"Failed to read summarize report; skipping local cleanup.", then silently
reports "Found 0 merged local branch(es)" and "Pruned 0 local branch(es)" as
if the repository were clean, and the follow-on remote prune also fails.
Observed during the AI_Hell v0.1.10 dev→main release; the same scripts succeed
when re-run standalone.

## Users

- **Agents (Map / herdr):** run automated releases and must not be misled by a
  false "clean" cleanup results.
- **Operators:** trust that post-release cleanup either happened or produced an
  actionable, non-silent warning.
- **Other projects consuming the shared ship/cleanup skills** (AI_Hell, etc.):
  any project can hit the race when releases coincide.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Post-release cleanup uses a **unique temp path per run** (e.g. derived from
   `mkdtempSync`) for the summarize report; a unit test with two
   concurrent-invocation fakes proves no shared-path clobber.
2. A failed `summarize_branches.py` run or report read no longer silently
   reports "0 merged branches" as if the repo were clean — it logs a distinct,
   actionable warning naming the deterministic remediation (unique temp path).
3. The cleanup stays **non-blocking**: a cleanup failure never changes the
   release exit code (existing AC3 preserved).
4. A transient failure (summarize run / report read / remote prune) is
   **retried once** before the actionable warning is emitted.

## Constraints

- Fix must live in the **SorraAgents** repo (ship/cleanup skills are symlinked
  from `~/.pi/agent/skills` into `SorraAgents/skill/`); AI_Hell does not vendor
  these files.
- Cleanup scripts' standalone behaviour (`summarize_branches.py`,
  `prune_local_branches.py`, `delete_remote_branches.py`) must not change.
- Non-blocking guarantee must be preserved (existing AC3 of
  SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG).
- Tests run under `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"` in SorraAgents.

## Existing state

`runPostReleaseCleanup` passes a fixed `${tempDir}/cleanup-summary.json` to
`summarize_branches.py --report` (~L1110) and reads it back (~L1135). On read
failure it sets `reportData = { branches: [] }` and logs only the generic
"skipping local cleanup" warning, then proceeds to report "Found 0 merged local
branch(es)". The branches-to-delete file already uses `mkdtempSync`
(`cleanup-branches-*`), so only the report path is shared.

## Desired change

- Derive a unique report path per run (mkdtemp-based) used for both the
  `--report` argument and the read-back, so concurrent runs cannot clobber.
- Distinguish a real "no merged branches" result from a failed enumerate/read:
  log an actionable warning (unique-path remediation) instead of the misleading
  "0 merged branches".
- Add a single retry with small backoff for the transient step(s) before
  emitting the warning, preserving non-blocking behaviour.
- Extend `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` with the concurrency-clobber
  test and report-failure-warning test.

## Key Files:

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `runPostReleaseCleanup` (report path
  L1110/L1135, retry logic, warning text)
- `tests/unit/test-run-release-cleanup.mjs` — new AC1 concurrency fake test,
  AC2 warning test, AC4 retry test

## Risks & assumptions

- **Retry must not mask real errors** — the single retry is for transient
  failures only; the actionable warning must still be emitted on the second
  failure (assumption: failures are quiet enough to retry once without
  doubling wall-clock time; mitigation: small backoff).
- **Scope creep** — deeper cleanup-skill refactoring, branch-deletion policy
  changes, or fixing `delete_remote_branches.py`/`summarize_branches.py`
  behaviour are out of scope; if such work is discovered, record it as new
  linked work items (not here).
- **Test isolation** — the concurrency test must not touch the real
  `/tmp/cleanup-summary.json` or run real git commands; fakes only
  (assumption: existing `setupRunReleaseFixture` harness is reused/adapted).
- **Cross-repo tracking** — item originated in the AI_Hell worklog
  (AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU, moved here per producer decision Q1c); AI_Hell leaves
  no orphan reference after deletion.
- **Non-blocking guarantee** — AC3 must survive the retry addition; the retry
  must also be non-blocking.

## Related work

- SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG — Automate post-release cleanup (introduced this code).
- AH-0MTXLWCWO005OSCZ — Discord notification fails (precedent: ship-skill bug
  tracked in AH worklog, fixed in SorraAgents).
- SA-0MUII5QDI005U2AH — Live-repo guard concurrency (related concurrency issue).
- SA-0MUJQ5BPF001PICU — Test-suite flakiness under concurrent agent load.
- discovered-from: AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU (moved from AI_Hell worklog);
  discovered-from: release-v0.1.10.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Where should the fix be implemented/tracked? The code lives in
  SorraAgents (ship/cleanup skills); this item is tracked in the AI_Hell
  worklog." — Answer (producer): **(c)** "check an equivalent doesn't already
  exist first, delete this item" (i.e. move the item entirely to SorraAgents).
  Source: interactive reply. Research: searched the SorraAgents worklog for
  `cleanup-summary`, `runPostReleaseCleanup`, `post-release cleanup`, `tmp
  path`, `shared report`, `concurrent agents`, `branch cleanup` — no equivalent
  open/closed item; only the completed feature SA-0MUV2W2P7004HVIG and two
  unrelated concurrency items. Outcome: created SA-0MV6JQP9K004QGUT here and
  deleted AH-0MUZGWL14001E1EU.
- Q2: "Is 'retry once' in scope? Expected Behaviour promises it but the ACs do
  not require it." — Answer (producer): **(a)** add it as AC4. Source:
  interactive reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS3ATINN006QT1M** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/cleanup/scripts/inspect_current_branch.py:28 — Do not catch blind exception: `Exception` (BLE001) (completed)
- **SA-0MS3ATJR7003CK2B** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/cleanup/scripts/prune_local_branches.py:38 — Do not catch blind exception: `Exception` (BLE001) (completed)
- **SA-0MSMT0B3E009NTB7** – [MEDIUM] /home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/tests/test_cleanup_scripts.py:1 — Import block is un-sorted or un-formatted (I001) (open)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+162 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance (+154 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance, actionable (+144 more)

## Impact

A release or cleanup run can no longer be misled into reporting a clean repository when its branch-enumeration report was clobbered by another concurrent run: each run now owns a unique report path, transient failures are retried once, and any remaining failure produces an actionable warning naming the remediation instead of a false "0 merged branches".

data.description:
## Objective

Make `/skill:ship release` judge the importance of the work items in the release and propose the semantically correct semver bump (patch, minor, or major), instead of always bumping patch — with the producer asked in the PI session before any non-patch bump is applied.

## Problem Statement

The ship skill currently always increments the `z` (patch) component of the release version (`merge-dev-to-main.sh` defaults `BUMP="patch"`), even when the release adds new or breaking capability. Releases that add features therefore ship as patch versions (e.g. `v0.1.19` instead of `v0.2.0`), misrepresenting the release's impact and forcing the producer to remember `--bump minor` manually.

## Users

- **Release manager (the PI agent running `/skill:ship release`)** — must judge the release's importance from the items being shipped and propose the right bump without extra flags.
- **Producer** — must see and approve any non-patch bump, in the session, with a full justification naming the items that triggered it.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when every item in the release is a fix, chore, or documentation change, I want the release to bump patch automatically so that I don't have to think about semver.
- As a release manager, when the release contains meaningful new capability, I want to propose a minor bump with evidence, rather than silently shipping it as a patch.
- As a producer, I want to be asked, in the session, before a minor or major bump is applied, with a justification naming the items and why they warrant the bump — and I want to be able to decline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ship skill's release workflow gains a startup **version-bump evaluation** step that runs before any git mutation and gathers every release candidate (`wl list --stage in_review`) with enough context for a judgement: ID, title, type, priority, `## Impact`/user story and a short description excerpt.
- The agent judges the importance of the release from those items and proposes exactly one bump: **patch** when the release only fixes, documents, or maintains; **minor** when it adds meaningful new capability; **major** when it breaks or removes existing capability or otherwise changes behaviour incompatibly (the existing `--bump` override remains available).
- A **patch** proposal proceeds automatically with no producer interaction — the current `--bump patch` behaviour and `merge-dev-to-main.sh` default are unchanged.
- A **minor or major** proposal prints a full justification — each contributing item ID and title, why it warrants the bump, and the proposed `old → new` version — and the agent asks the producer **in the PI session**; no git mutation, tag, PR, or worklog close occurs until the producer approves.
- Producer approval proceeds with the approved `--bump`; a declined non-patch proposal is honoured (the agent does not apply it, and records the decision and the producer's preferred bump in the session and on the release's work item).
- In a non-interactive/headless context where the producer cannot be asked, a minor or major proposal is never auto-approved: the agent records the justification, flags the item for producer review, and stops.
- The judgement is based on the release items' content (Impact/description/capability), not on `issueType` or a label lookup; the justification cites the evidence used.
- Minor bumps reset `z` to `0`, and major bumps reset `y` and `z` to `0`, reusing the existing `release/bump-version.js` semantics rather than duplicating version arithmetic.
- Unit tests cover: candidate gathering (including an empty candidate set), the review packet/justification rendering, patch auto-proceed, and the non-patch approval-pending behaviour (no mutation); no test reads or mutates the live worklog.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`, and code comments.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Releases that add or break capability will carry a version number that reflects it, and producers will be asked in-session to approve that call with evidence instead of policing `--bump` flags by hand.

## Existing State

- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` sets `BUMP="patch"` by default and accepts `--bump patch|minor|major` (already validates the value).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` parses and forwards `--bump` to the merge script; the wrapper has no bump evaluation step and its documented exit codes are `0`–`14`.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` already implements `patch`/`minor`/`major` arithmetic correctly (including `z = 0` on minor and `y = z = 0` on major) and resolves `package.json` or `pyproject.toml` as the version source.
- Release candidates are items with `stage: in_review` (`check-audit-gate.js::getCandidateItems`), so the candidate set already exists.
- The release wrapper subprocess is non-interactive, but the ship skill itself is a PI skill executed by an agent in a session — the agent, not the shell script, is the component that can ask the producer.

## Desired Change

1. Add a small, unit-testable helper (e.g. `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js`) that gathers release candidates and renders a compact review packet: per item `id`, `title`, `issueType`, `priority`, `## Impact` (or user story) and a truncated description excerpt, plus the current version and the three candidate bump outcomes. It gathers and renders only — no judgement, no mutation.
2. Add a "Version bump evaluation" step at the start of the documented release workflow in `skill/ship/SKILL.md` (before gates and merge): run the preflight, judge the release's importance, and choose patch/minor/major.
3. Patch → run the release normally (patch is the existing default).
4. Minor/major → present the justification to the producer in the session and wait for approval; on approval run `run-release.js --bump <approved>`; on decline, do not apply.
5. Keep the judgement rationale and the producer's decision in the session output and, where the release is tied to a work item, in a comment so the version choice is auditable.
6. Update `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and the SKILL.md workflow/argument docs to describe the evaluation step and the in-session approval gate.

## Constraints

- **Judgement stays with the agent:** no issue-type or label mapping, and no mechanical classifier is added — the evaluation prompt/rubric is documented, and the agent makes the call from the items' content.
- **Producer gates non-patch bumps:** minor and major bumps must never be applied without an explicit producer approval in the session. Patch bumps stay automatic.
- **Fail-closed in headless runs:** where no producer is available (downtime/automated dispatches), a minor/major proposal must stop with producer review rather than self-approve.
- **Backward compatible:** an explicit `--bump` keeps its current meaning and precedence; invoking `merge-dev-to-main.sh` directly keeps its `patch` default.
- **No duplicated version arithmetic:** reuse `bump-version.js` for the actual bump; the new code only gathers evidence and renders the proposal.
- **Fail-safe:** an unreadable/empty candidate set must default to patch with a warning and must never block a release that would otherwise succeed; a preflight failure must not mutate the repository.
- **No live-worklog test access:** unit tests must inject the candidate-fetch boundary.
- **Auditability:** the proposed and approved bump, the justification, and the producer's decision are recorded (session output plus a work-item comment for item-linked releases).

## Key Files

- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — new "Version bump evaluation" workflow step, in-session approval gate, argument/behaviour docs.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-preflight.js` — new candidate-gathering/review-packet helper (and its tests).
- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — unchanged `--bump` forwarding, plus any logging of the decided bump; verify no new git side effects.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh` — receives the decided `--bump`; default unchanged.
- `skill/ship/scripts/release/bump-version.js` — reused as-is for arithmetic (verify minor resets patch to `0`, major resets minor and patch).
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — `getCandidateItems` is the release-candidate source.
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — reference for the evaluation step and approval gate.
- `skill/ship/tests/` — new unit tests for the preflight helper and the approval-pending path.

## Related Work

- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** — Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (introduced the bump step and `v<semver>` tag convention).
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** — ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (version source resolution).
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** — Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs.
- **SA-0MQI6MDUP001S8NL** — bump-version.js isMainModule check fails on symlinked install paths.
- **SA-0MRGVN9XM003LNQ7** — Close work items when shipping (uses the released version in `Shipped in v<version>` markers).
- **SA-0MV0PZYMI004SUFR** — Newly-created-tag gate (precedent for a fail-closed startup gate with a distinct exit code).
- **SA-0MUIVIJFT0009ZNV** — Missing-script fail-fast (precedent for refusing early, before any git/worklog side effects).

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Judgement subjectivity (risk):** "meaningful new capability" is a judgement call, and two agents could judge the same release differently. Mitigation: a documented rubric (new capability → minor, breaking change → major, fixes/docs/maintenance only → patch), the evidence-based justification, and the producer's in-session approval for every non-patch bump.
- **Producer availability (risk):** a headless release cannot ask anyone. Mitigation: a non-patch proposal in a headless run stops with producer review instead of self-approving; patch releases are unaffected.
- **Agent discipline (risk):** the gate lives in the documented workflow, so a release run by bypassing the skill (direct `run-release.js`) is not gated. Mitigation: document the workflow as the canonical path, and keep the version arithmetic and safety gates in the script unchanged.
- **Scope-creep risk:** per-item bump annotations, automatic CHANGELOG grouping, and mechanical classification are separate opportunities and should be filed as follow-up items rather than folded into this change.
- **Empty candidate set:** a release with no `in_review` items (e.g. hotfix) defaults to patch and logs why.
- **`--skip-checks` interaction (assumption):** `--skip-checks` bypasses branch/critical gates only; the bump evaluation still runs, and an explicit `--bump` remains an operator override.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions and answers

- **Q1 (basis for minor-worthiness):** How should the release's importance be judged?
  - Options considered: (A) by `issueType`; (B) by `priority`; (C) by an explicit label/tag; (D) the agent's interpretation of the items' importance.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's not about issue type or label. It's about your interpretation of the importance of the items in the release. Make the best call you can. Check with the producer." → **Option D**, with a documented rubric and producer confirmation.
- **Q2 (approval mechanism):** How is the producer asked to approve a proposed minor/major bump?
  - Options considered: (A) fail-closed exit code + producer re-runs with `--bump`; (B) an interactive prompt inside the PI session; (C) automatic bump with a warning.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "It's a skill in PI, ask in the session." → **Option B**: the agent presents the justification and asks the producer in the session; the subprocess itself stays non-interactive.
- **Q3 (major inference):** Should a `major` (x) bump be inferred?
  - Options considered: (A) no — only minor/patch; (B) infer and suggest major, but never apply without producer approval.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-14):** "You can infer it and suggest it, but never implement without checking with the producer." → **Option B**: major may be proposed and justified, gated by the same in-session producer approval as minor.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPYO85WW006CXPL** – Add version numbering to ship skill for releases (completed)
- **SA-0MRB2FB5X008X4MM** – Fix bump-version.js REPO_ROOT resolution for global skill installs (completed)
- **SA-0MVN2B0DJ00135W0** – ship: bump-version.js must support Python projects (pyproject.toml version source) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: able, acceptance, accepts, access, actual (+331 more)
- `docs/dev/implement-skill-reference.md` — matched: able, acceptance, actual, add, added (+325 more)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — matched: able, acceptance, accepts, actual, add (+325 more)

- Test name: skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py::test_concurrent_finishes_overlap_their_full_suite_runs
- Failing commit: (not available)

```
Finish gate (full-scope fallback) failed: test_concurrent_finishes_overlap_their_full_suite_runs. Unrelated to the ship cleanup change under test (run-release.js); the test exercises concurrent implement finish lock behaviour and is load-sensitive (see SA-0MWFJRWN00084FE1).
```

## Steps To Reproduce

1. Checkout the commit: `git checkout <commit-hash>`
2. Run the failing test: `pytest -q -r a --disable-warnings -k skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py::test_concurrent_finishes_overlap_their_full_suite_runs` (or equivalent command)
3. Capture full logs and attach to the work item

1. The test `skill/implement/tests/test_finish_main_checkout_lock.py::test_concurrent_finishes_overlap_their_full_suite_runs` passes when run against the latest `dev`.
2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.
3. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

1. Verify flakiness: rerun CI/test locally once.
2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.
3. If flaky, tag `flaky` and route to flaky-test queue.
